text:
support_eng: Customer (acme.io) opened an urgent ticket — EU users hitting 502s and huge latency, but their route is pinned to eu-west. They report requests going to us-east and auth failures. Billing spike too :grimacing:
lee_sre: Can you paste the route/failover policy they have? thread_ts pls and sample request ids
support_eng: Ticket ID #4529. Sample request id: req_0a3f. Policy payload from console (pasted from customer):
```json
{
  "routes": [
    { "region": "us-east", "priority": "10", "weight": "100", "sticky": true },
    { "region": "eu-west", "priority": "2", "weight": "50", "sticky": true }
  ]
}
```
sam_devex: Uh — priorities are strings. We sort priority arrays client-side as numbers, but console merge sometimes writes strings; if sorting is lexicographic, "10" < "2" which would flip ordering. That would make us prefer us-east.
maria_prod: Also seeing in audit logs a recent console merge at 2689989000 by product-batch-import which flattened numbers to strings during a bulk update. ops-bot: deploy/commit 2026-03-15T11:02:33 finished (config service).
lee_sre: That explains cross-region hits and the auth failures — eu keys are scoped to eu region; when requests land in us-east they hit auth mismatch, return 401s and sometimes 502s on our gateway when route TTL mismatch occurs. Any evidence of sticky cookie behavior?
support_eng: Customer logs show Set-Cookie: rw_route=eu-west; Domain=.acme.io sometimes missing, then cookie bounced between regions. They also reported sticky:true in both entries.
maria_prod: The bug is twofold: 1) priority stored as strings so ordering flipped, 2) sticky cookies lacking domain from our SDK patch, so sessions lost and failover triggered to the now-high-priority us-east region => auth 401s and gateway 502 retries.
lee_sre: Repro steps? Can we replay a request with their header set and confirm hit region?
sam_devex: Repro snippet: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <eu-key>" -H "Host: api.acme.io" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?route_id=acme-eu" -c /tmp/cookies.txt -b /tmp/cookies.txt
```
Do 5 requests in a row. On my run, 1st goes to eu-west, then after policy merge to us-east and cookie mismatch I saw 502 + 401s.
lee_sre: Good. Can we confirm config service stores priorities as strings? query: `SELECT key,value FROM config_kv WHERE route_id='acme-eu'`
maria_prod: Ran that: value contains the JSON with "priority":"10" etc. I'll push a migration to coerce numeric fields to ints and normalize weights. Patch: 
```sql
UPDATE config_kv
SET value = regexp_replace(value, '"priority":\s*"(\d+)"', '"priority": \1')
WHERE route_id='acme-eu';
```
ops-bot: config-service rollout started (canary) 3 nodes
support_eng: Customer is high-touch — escalating to accounts for billing spike, can we prepare a credit statement? Lina_billing?
lina_billing: I'll flag acct team and draft a credit for the minutes of cross-region egress + token retries. Need final numbers from infra.
lee_sre: Immediate mitigation: 1) Temporarily set explicit region-lock for acme-eu to eu-west in routing table (force) 2) Disable sticky for that customer until cookie domain fix 3) rollback config-service commit that stringified numbers.
maria_prod: Doing steps: pushed forced route via admin API and disabled sticky for route id acme-eu. Rolling back the bad deploy on canary in progress.
ops-bot: rollback/config-service to previous commit initiated
support_eng: Customer confirmed latency drops after forced lock, they still see some 502s for the next 2 minutes — probably queued retries.
sam_devex: After migration, echoed normalized policy: 
```json
{
  "routes": [
    { "region": "eu-west", "priority": 2, "weight": 50, "sticky": false },
    { "region": "us-east", "priority": 10, "weight": 100, "sticky": false }
  ]
}
```
lee_sre: Next actions: 1) full config migration to convert any stringified numeric fields 2) add unit test to console bulk-import to preserve number types 3) add a quick alert when route priority ordering results in non-numeric compare (detect lexicographic flip)
maria_prod: I'll open PRs for migration + tests and schedule a postmortem doc.
lina_billing: I'll send provisional credit draft to accounts and cc support.
support_eng: Closing loop with customer: we provided mitigation, ETA for full fix ~3 hours, offering credits. Customer accepted temporary lock and asked for postmortem.
lee_sre: Filing incident ticket INC-2026-017 for tracking. Marking severity P2->P1 during mitigation window.
support_eng: Thanks team :heart: — keep updates in this thread; will paste final postmortem link here when ready.
